pageCache.pageTitle: West Ham Church School and Little Owls Nursery – With God, all things are possible – Matthew 19:26
pageCache.text:
A warm welcome to West Ham Church Primary School.
Situated in the heart of Newham, within the Diocese of Chelmsford, West Ham Church Primary School is a vibrant, values-led community where every child is known, loved, and encouraged to flourish.
Our vision sits at the heart of all we do. Guided by our Christian values of Wonder, Harmony, Compassion, and Strength, we nurture each child to grow in faith, curiosity, confidence, and character.
We are proud of our rich diversity and the strong sense of belonging that unites our children, families, and staff. Rooted in Christian values and open to all, our school community welcomes children from every background, faith, and culture. We believe our diversity is a blessing and that learning from one another builds understanding, respect, and harmony.
We aim to provide a safe, happy, and stimulating environment where children experience Wonder in learning, work in Harmony with others, show Compassion in their actions, and develop the Strength to persevere and succeed. Our broad and ambitious curriculum inspires curiosity and creativity while supporting every child to achieve their full potential — academically, socially, and spiritually.
Our dedicated staff team works in close partnership with parents, governors, and the wider community to create a nurturing, inspiring learning experience. Together, we celebrate each child as an individual and encourage them to make a positive difference in the world.
Whether you are a current parent, a prospective family, or a visitor, I hope this website offers you a glimpse into what makes West Ham Church Primary School such a special place. We warmly invite you to visit us and see our vision and values brought to life through our wonderful children every day.
Mrs James Headteacher

Character Development at WHCS
At West Ham Church of England Primary School, we believe that a child’s character is just as important to their future happiness and success as academic achievement.
We aim to empower every child with the tools to grow into kind, courageous, thoughtful and resilient individuals, ready to make a positive impact on the world around them.
At West Ham Church Primary School, our core values of Wonder, Harmony, Compassion, and Strength are at the heart of everything we do. They guide how we learn, how we treat one another, and how we grow, both as individuals and as a community.
These values shape every aspect of school life, helping children to thrive in all aspects of life by nurturing their growth into well-rounded, empathetic individuals who positively contribute to and shape society and the wider world.
To enable children, with God’s guidance, to know and appreciate the wonder of God’s creation, to live in harmony embracing differences, to always act with compassion inspired by the example of Jesus, and to have the strength to follow their dreams and achieve their goals.

Character Days at West Ham Church Primary School
At West Ham Church Primary School, we are proud to focus on Character Days throughout the year, each one focused on one of our core values: Wonder, Harmony, Compassion, and Strength.
These special days give children the opportunity to explore each value in depth through creative, refl ective, and hands-on activities.
Whether it’s engaging in science and nature investigations for Wonder, team-building and music for Harmony, community outreach and storytelling for Compassion, or resilience challenges and inspirational role models for Strength—each day is designed to bring our values to life in meaningful ways.
Character Days help our pupils connect what they learn in the classroom to the kind of people they are becoming, strengthening our whole-school culture of kindness, curiosity, and moral integrity.
Student leadership opportunities
At West Ham Church School, we are deeply committed to developing every child as a confi dent, responsible, and compassionate leader who lives out our core values of Wonder, Harmony, Compassion, and Strength.
Pupils are given a wide range of opportunities to lead, serve, and make a positive difference within our school community. Our Head Pupils and House Captains act as role models of integrity and teamwork, supporting school events and encouraging younger pupils to embody our Christian values.
The School Council ( KS1- KS2) provides a strong pupil voice, allowing children to share ideas and contribute to decisions that shape school life. Collective Worship Leaders play a vital role in planning and leading worship, promoting spiritual refl ection and our Christian ethos.
Our Playground Leaders help ensure playtimes are happy and inclusive, modelling kindness and friendship, while Junior Travel Ambassadors promote road safety and sustainable travel. Young Interpreters support new pupils and families who speak English as an additional language, helping everyone feel welcome and valued.
The Librarians from year 6 nurture a love of reading across the school, maintaining our library and recommending books that inspire curiosity and wonder.
Together, these roles empower pupils to develop confi dence, empathy, responsibility, and teamwork — preparing them to be thoughtful, active citizens who contribute positively to their community and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: History – West Ham Church School and Little Owls Nursery
pageCache.text:
We are 300 years old! We celebrated our tercentenary in December 2023 with a special Christingle Service at All Saints Church including a huge cake and candles, balloons and, of course, singing. We are proud to continue to serve our rich and diverse local community.
West Ham Church School opened in 1723 as the first parish charity school in West Ham and also the first school to open in what is now the Newham area. It was held in the porch of the neighbouring All Saints church to teach the poor children of Plaistow and Stratford to read and it was attended by 10 boys. Girls were first admitted two years later in 1725.
By 1731 the school had secured its own building east of the church yard and by 1752 a second school building was added to the north of the original building called the ‘School of Industry’. In 1769, the ‘School of Industry’ started to be used by the owners of Sarah Bonnell’s girls’ school, so both Sarah Bonnell’s and West Ham Church School shared the same site.
The school’s shield comes from Sir John Henry Pelly, the first baronet of Upton, who was the school’s treasurer. In 1861, when a new boy’s block was built, the building was first known as the Pelly Memorial.
In 1871 the West Ham Church School roll was then 330 in the boy’s school, 130 in the girl’s department and 190 infants.
By 1876 Sarah Bonnell’s School (also known at the time as West Ham High School for girls) had moved to West Ham Lane. It was mainly for fee-paying girls, but free places were reserved for West Ham Church School girls.
In 1934 West Ham Church School became a mixed infant and junior school.
In 1964, West Ham Church School was completely rebuilt after being damaged in the war. The pictures below are of the old building before it was destroyed. They were found on display in the local library.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupil Leadership – West Ham Church School and Little Owls Nursery
pageCache.text:
Our school is divided into four Houses, each named after a part of the British Isles: England, Scotland, Wales, and Ireland.
At the beginning of each school year, House Captains are elected by their peers in Year 6. These students are role models and leaders within our school community.
They inspire others by encouraging house spirit, collecting and tallying house points, and leading various events, including Sports Day and other team-building activities throughout the year.
Every Tuesday, during our Achievement Assembly, House Captains announce the weekly house point winner. Our leadership team, along with the students, also lead a variety of assemblies throughout the year, where we explore current affairs, significant events, and Bible stories.
Throughout the year, students earn house points for their efforts, which are celebrated during our Friday Celebration Assembly. It’s always an exciting moment as we reveal which house is in the lead and who will be the winner for the week!
With God, all things are possible – Matthew 19:26
At West Ham Church School, the Worship Leaders, are committed to ensuring that everyone has the opportunity to engage in inspiring, exciting, and meaningful Collective Worship. We also strive to create calm, reflective spaces for everyone to enjoy. We see it as our responsibility to be ambassadors of the school’s Christian values, setting a positive example for others through our behaviour, interactions, and leadership.
Being a Worship Leader involves monitoring Collective Worship, providing feedback on what we and our fellow students have enjoyed, and suggesting things we’d like to see more of. We take an active role in planning and leading worship, which includes reading Bible passages, praying prayers we have written, and sharing prayers written by our classmates.
In addition, we assist in setting up for Collective Worship. We prepare PowerPoint slides, select calming music to help set the tone as children enter, and organise the song of the day. We also support with storytelling, acting out stories, or reading passages aloud to the school community.

The School Council meets at least once a half term. The meetings are led and minuted by the member of staff responsible for the School Council.

pageCache.pageTitle: Research and Innovation – West Ham Church School and Little Owls Nursery
pageCache.text:
At West Ham Church School, we are committed to evidence-informed practice and have proudly taken part in a number of national research projects. These completed studies have enriched our understanding of teaching and learning, improved outcomes for our pupils, and contributed to the broader educational research community. Several of these were rigorously evaluated by the Education Endowment Foundation (EEF).
Maths Through Picture Books (EEF-evaluated)
We took part in this project to investigate how high-quality picture books can be used to support the development of early mathematical understanding. By linking stories to mathematical ideas, children engaged with number and problem-solving in creative, meaningful ways.
Children’s University (EEF-evaluated)
This project encouraged pupils to take part in exciting and enriching learning activities beyond the classroom—such as clubs, trips, and creative challenges. Our participation supported research into how such activities can raise aspirations and foster a lifelong love of learning.
Mathematical Reasoning in Year 2 (EEF-evaluated)
This study focused on developing pupils’ ability to explain and justify their mathematical thinking. As part of this EEF project, we introduced structured reasoning tasks in Year 2, helping children build stronger mathematical understanding and confidence.
Stop and Think (with NatCen Social Research)
Delivered in partnership with NatCen Social Research, this project focused on metacognition—teaching children to pause, reflect, and think carefully before responding. It aimed to improve learning outcomes by developing children’s reasoning and decision-making skills.
Infant Language Link
This intervention enabled us to assess speech and language development in younger pupils, identify those needing support, and deliver targeted activities to strengthen language skills—particularly important in the early years of schooling.
We took part in the ICICLES project, which explored the impact of Covid-19 on children’s language, educational progress, and social-emotional wellbeing. Our involvement helped researchers better understand how the pandemic affected young learners, and what support is most effective in helping them recover and thrive.
NELI (Nuffield Early Language Intervention)
As part of the national rollout of NELI, we implemented this evidence-based programme in our Reception classes. It helped children with communication difficulties improve their vocabulary, listening, and narrative skills—setting them up for success in school.
Through our involvement in these important projects, West Ham Church School continues to champion research-informed education and ensure that all pupils benefit from strategies proven to make a real difference.

pageCache.pageTitle: Safeguarding – West Ham Church School and Little Owls Nursery
pageCache.text:
Safeguarding at West Ham Church School
Our priority is safety and we want our children and staff to feel that they are listened to. We have a culture where all staff understand that safeguarding is the responsibility of all staff. Please read our Child Protection and Safeguarding Policy. We have adopted the London Borough of Newham’s policy, which complies with the Department of Education’s Keeping Children Safe in Education document. Our Photography and Filming Policy Statement has been adapted from the NSPCC model policy.
All staff receive in depth safeguarding training annually, with updated informationduring the year. Staff and volunteers are recruited in line with Safer Recruitment Procedures, therefore all appropriate checks are completed. Anyone visiting the school for thefirst time will receive our safeguarding and evacuation procedures. Visual informationregarding our safeguarding team is displayed throughout our school.
Any safeguarding concerns must be reported to the safeguarding team immediately.Concerns regarding a member of staff should be reported to the head teacher or theLocal Authority Designated Officer (LADO), who can be contacted on 0203 373 3392 or email CPRT.LADO@newham.gov.uk.
Our Safeguarding Governor is Ms Manion-Krase.
We are partners in the joint London Metropolitan Police and London borough of Newham’s Operation Encompass, a confidential channel of communication between the police and Key Adults within the school (Safeguarding Team). The Key Adult is contacted securely if the police attend a domestic abuse incident with children in the household. This enables early intervention and further support in school to address the broader effects of the abuse.
We also work with a range of specialists to support pupils including an Educational Psychologist and an Art Therapist. Information on how to support children experiencing safeguarding issues can be found on the following websites:

pageCache.pageTitle: Admissions – West Ham Church School and Little Owls Nursery
pageCache.text:
Children are accepted onto the West Ham Church School Nursery admissions list from their 2nd birthday and can start Nursery, Little Owls, when they are 3 years old.
We offer morning and afternoon sessions in our Little Owls Nursery:
Morning: from 8:30am – 11:30am (autumn, spring and summer terms)
Afternoon: from 12:30pm – 3:30pm (spring and summer terms)
You can click on the link to apply for our Nursery or call into the school for a paper application.
30 Hour places are also available subject to confirmation of your entitlement code.
Most children transition into our reception, although when demand is high we cannot guarantee a place. Those parents who wish their children to transfer to the school should send their application forms to the London Borough of Newham by the appropriate deadline. Please speak to our office staff if you need advice.
Joining the school later
Some children join the school later on or mid-term. If this is the case, parents are invited to meet the Family Support Worker/Learning Mentor and in some cases, the Headteacher. New pupils are assigned a Buddy in their new class and can attend Nurture club at lunchtimes with the Learning Mentor to help them settle.
Moving on – Secondary School Transfer
The transition from primary to secondary schooling can be a difficult and stressful time for parents and children. In order to minimise this, we run meetings for parents to help to explain the application process and to offer help and advice about gaining entry to the school of their choice.
Visits are also made to West Ham Church School by staff from the local secondary schools who talk to the Year 6 children and answer their questions and concerns about secondary school life. Transition day visits to the children’s new schools usually occur during the summer term.
If a child is not allocated a school place and parents wish to appeal this decision, please contact the London Borough of Newham for more information.

pageCache.pageTitle: Attendance – West Ham Church School and Little Owls Nursery
pageCache.text:
Due to school closure from March to July 2020, many children missed out on lessons which has left them vulnerable to falling behind with their learning. Pupils need to attend school regularly to benefit from their education. Children with poor attendance tend to achieve less and have less opportunity for good outcomes in the future.
For children to gain the greatest benefit from their education it is vital that they attend regularly, and your child should be at school in good time for the start of the school day, every day the school is open, unless they are genuinely ill. Our Attendance Policy represents our commitment to striving for 100% attendance.
The school’s Attendance Policy principles:
These principles are enshrined in British law, within the Education Act 1996, the Children Act 1989, and other associated pieces of legislation.
It is imperative that children arrive at school on time to make the most of every learning opportunity. All children are to be dropped off at the back gates. If you are experiencing issues with punctuality, we suggest your child attends our Breakfast club so they are well-prepared and ready for the school day.
Reporting your child’s absence
If your child is absent, you must:
Applications for leave of absence in term time
Policy is not to authorise leave of absence from school during term time. Any applications for leave in term time must be made in writing to the Headteacher. There is no automatic right to term time leave of absence, and your request is likely to be declined except in the most exceptional circumstances. Each application will be considered on its own merit, and the attendance record(s) of the child/ren concerned will be taken into account when making a decision.
Penalty Notices can now be issued for a range of attendance-related offences, including unauthorised term-time holidays, poor attendance and poor punctuality, or being out in a public place without justification during the first five days of an exclusion. Further details are available on www.newham.gov.uk/schools/Attendance.

We operate a soft start at the beginning of the day, starting from 8:30am, with gates closing at 8:45am.

Arrive 8:30-8:45am Depart 3:15pm
Kindly note, if your child has a place booked in the Breakfast Club at 7:30am, please do not use the main entrance, but bring your child to our back gate on St. Lucia Drive.
We also run a Bagel Grab’n’go club that starts from 8:15am.
At the end of the school day, parents/carers use the playground to wait for the children to be dismissed. Please note, we will not release the children to anyone who is not on the approved collection list, so please contact the school office to let us know if you need any changes to be made to the list or if you will be late to collect your child.
Travelling to school
In line with government advice, we strongly encourage parents to walk their children to school and avoid travelling on public transport. Parking and congestion on the roads near the school can become heavy at critical times such as school opening and school closing, so we ask parents and carers to walk to school. If driving is unavoidable, we ask you to park a little further away from the school and walk a few metres with your child/ren in order to help to ease the congestion.
A secure bike shed is available for children to leave their bikes during the day. Please telephone and speak to the School Business Manager or Admin staff if you would like to make use of this facility.
The school provides a hot lunch for each child cooked on site by our catering company, Juniper Ventures. Children have their lunch served in the hall.
https://www.juniperventures.co.uk/education-catering/primary-school-catering/
Cool Fuel for School
All the menus prepared each day will always exceed the Government’s tough Food based guidelines and we are very proud of our menus being independently assessed by the Soil Association as meeting their Food for Life standards. This means that you can be assured that over 80% of the food we serve is cooked from fresh ingredients each day. Our menus are made up of seasonable, fully traceable, healthier, sustainable and fresh ingredients that are free from trans-fats and nasty additives.
We want to make lunchtime fun and will often hold interesting and exciting Discovery Day lunches in partnership with the school focussing on national events or curriculum-based themes.
As part of our programme of encouraging healthier eating there is always an unlimited supply of vegetables and salad available for every child each day.
Please inform the school if your child has any special dietary requirements or dietary allergies. Children with food allergies and special dietary requirements wear particular items to ensure that they are easily identified.
Every primary school aged child attending school in Newham still has the opportunity to have a free school lunch even if their parents/carers are not in receipt of one of the qualifying benefits for free school meals. For more information on Newham’s Eat for Free click here.
Eligibility for free school meals
Your child may receive free school meals if you get any of the following benefits:
We strongly encourage children to have a hot school meal to try new flavours and textures and broaden their eating experience. If you decide to give your child a packed lunch, we do enforce strict guidelines in regards to contents of the packed lunch. We do not allow crisps, sweets, chocolate or flavoured drinks.
Please note: Nuts are not allowed in school as we have several children and staff who are allergic to nuts.
Fruit, Milk and Water
Milk is provided free of charge to nursery children. A piece of fruit is also provided daily through the Government’s fruit scheme for children in Reception and KS1 (Years 1 and 2). Children in KS2 (Year 3 – Year 6) are able to bring in fruit from home for their own mid-morning break if you wish them to.
The school encourages children to drink water throughout the day and all children are provided with a free water bottle when they first join the school. Please ensure that bottles are clearly marked with your child’s name. Bottles are sent home to be cleaned and refilled each evening and should be returned to school the next day.
Illness in school time
If your child becomes ill during the school day, s/he will be looked after by the school’s Welfare Assistant or first aiders and if it is necessary you will be contacted. It is therefore important that the school has up-to-date contact details and numbers for parents/carers.
Educational visits are a major part of your child’s education and school life. Charges will only be made for a school activity if it is the only way to guarantee that the event takes place. This will usually include: individual music tuition, most visits and excursions, residential visits or some school clubs. Parents will always be informed of this at the outset and we will try to assist those parents who have genuine difficulty in paying. Read the full Charging Policy on our Policies page.
Children are not permitted to bring any items of value to school such as expensive clothes, toys, watches, mobile phones or large sums of money. The school does not accept responsibility for the loss or damage of any such items if they are brought into school.
No jewellery or nail varnish should be worn to school. Bangles or bracelets which are worn for religious reasons should be covered by a sweatband during PE, games and swimming.
Children with pierced ears may wear one pair of plain studs. These will need to be removed for PE, games or swimming or be covered with a plaster provided by parents for PE and/or swimming.
Volunteer at West Ham Church School
We warmly welcome expressions of interest from those who would like to volunteer at West Ham Church School.
Volunteers play a valuable role in enriching the life of our school community. By offering your time and skills, you not only contribute to the quality of our pupils’ education, but also have the opportunity to develop your own experience and expertise.
Do you have a passion for a particular subject? Whether it’s reading, maths, or another area of interest, we would love to hear from you—especially if you’re keen to provide additional support to our pupils.
If you’re interested in volunteering, please contact the school office to request an application form. Successful applicants will be invited for an informal interview. Depending on the nature of the role, an enhanced DBS check may be required.
West Ham Church School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, and we expect all staff and volunteers to share this commitment.
Parent Consultations
Parent consultations are held three times per year to give teachers the opportunity to feedback to parents on their children’s progress and for parents to pass on information relating to their child or to address any concerns with the teachers. There are also a number of phase meetings which are specially arranged for parents as appropriate throughout the year.
We try to hold regular coffee mornings with the Headteacher, the Business Manager, the school nurse or other special visitors who speak on educational issues or advise parents on diet, exercise or child health.
Our Nursery, Little Owls, also hold regular coffee mornings on Fridays.

pageCache.pageTitle: How to Help Your Child – West Ham Church School and Little Owls Nursery
pageCache.text:
Home learning is sent out weekly during term time and we encourage parents to support their children.
Please ensure your child has their logins for:
Please read to and read with your children regularly and encourage them to read independently. We suggest having a regular bedtime storytelling time to enjoy books together. Please use your child’s Reading Record book to keep a list of the books read.
Number bonds and times tables (multiplication and division) are important foundations of further maths knowledge. Without a thorough knowledge of these rules, children will struggle with maths later on. Please help them to learn their number bonds, multiplication and their division tables. Start with the easy tables first: 2, 5, 10, 11 x tables – before moving onto the others.
Encourage children to write as often as possible and to form their letters correctly. They could write about things they have done or places they have visited. They could also write diaries, book reviews or creative stories. Keep a scrapbook of holiday places visited and of course include your children’s comments on the events.
Teachers set targets for children in reading, writing and maths which are shared during parent consultations and end of year reports. Please check these and support your child at home to achieve them. Your child’s teacher will advise you on ways to help.v
The school runs a parenting course at intervals giving useful tips and advice to parents and carers. The course is run over an eight week period and led by the schools Learning Mentor/Family Support Worker. Parents who attended the last series of meetings found it a useful and informative resource and I would recommend it to parents who are able to attend next time it is run.
Please check the Useful Links page for children and parents as these contain many carefully selected websites. The websites for children cover many areas of the curriculum and should prove useful as homework aids or as important general knowledge. General knowledge is an important aspect of comprehension. All of the websites are presented in fun, colourful and informative ways. New links will be added as they are discovered.
